nodes.description: Public boolean state variable controlling whether minting is paused (defaults to true).
Public base URI string used for token metadata concatenation.
Public token metadata file extension, default '.json'.
Public provenance hash string for the collection.
Public mint price per token in wei, default 0.077 ether.
Public maximum number of tokens that can ever be minted (9444).
Public maximum number of tokens mintable in a single transaction (20).
Public counter of tokens minted so far, incremented in mintInternal.
Public starting index offset used for metadata shuffling.
Public _DateTime struct holding the public mint start date.
Public _DateTime struct holding the whitelist mint start date.
msg.sender: caller-controlled address used for owner checks, payments and randomness.
block.timestamp: miner-influenceable time source used for mint windows and randomness.
onlyOwner function that derives initialTokenId from keccak256(block.timestamp, msg.sender) modulo maxSupply.
Internal minting routine: checks supply, loops calling _safeMint and then increments tokenId.
Public payable mint function validating msg.value against cost and maxMintAmount before minting.
onlyOwner mint function passing msg.sender as recipient to mintInternal.
onlyOwner function sending the entire contract balance to msg.sender via low-level send.
Public payable burn function requiring caller to be the owner of the given token.
View function comparing block.timestamp against the public mint date.
View function comparing block.timestamp against the whitelist mint date.
View function building the metadata URI, applying the initialTokenId shift.
onlyOwner function updating the public mint date struct.
onlyOwner function updating the whitelist mint date struct.
onlyOwner function updating the mint cost.
onlyOwner function updating the maximum supply.
onlyOwner function toggling the paused state variable.
View function returning the tokenId counter.
Unsafe operation: _safeMint invokes onERC721Received on the recipient contract, enabling reentrancy.
Unsafe operation: payable(msg.sender).send(address(this).balance) forwards native currency.
Unsafe operation: arithmetic check tokenId + _mintAmount <= maxSupply and update tokenId += _mintAmount.
Unsafe operation: arithmetic comparison msg.value >= cost * _mintAmount.
Unsafe operation: keccak256(block.timestamp, msg.sender) % maxSupply used as pseudo-random token index.
Unsafe operation: token id computed as (tokenId + i) % maxSupply inside the mint loop.
_to: recipient address parameter of mintInternal, mint and mintOwner.
_mintAmount: number of tokens requested by the mint/mintOwner caller.
_tokenId: token identifier parameter of burn and tokenURI.
_newCost: new price parameter of setCost.
_newMaxSupply: new supply cap parameter of setMaxSupply.
_newBaseURI: new metadata base parameter of setBaseURI.
i: loop counter over the mint batch in mintInternal.
finalTotenId: shifted token id computed in tokenURI using initialTokenId.

edges.reason: mint() consumes the _mintAmount parameter when validating cost and calling mintInternal.
mint() forwards the caller-supplied _to recipient into mintInternal.
mint() performs cost * _mintAmount multiplication and compares it with msg.value.
mint() invokes mintInternal after payment validation.
The cost state variable is read and multiplied by _mintAmount in the payment check.
maxMintAmount state variable bounds the _mintAmount accepted by mint().
mintInternal checks tokenId + _mintAmount against maxSupply and then increments tokenId.
tokenId state variable participates in the supply arithmetic and is written back.
maxSupply state variable bounds the tokenId arithmetic in mintInternal.
mintInternal computes (tokenId + i) % maxSupply to derive each minted token id.
The loop index i feeds the (tokenId + i) % maxSupply token id computation.
mintInternal calls _safeMint which performs an external onERC721Received callback to the recipient contract before tokenId is fully synced.
The attacker-controlled _to address is the target of the _safeMint callback.
mintOwner() calls mintInternal directly.
mintOwner() passes msg.sender as the mint recipient, relying on the caller identity.
mintOwner() supplies msg.sender as the _to parameter of mintInternal.
setInitialTokenId builds the initial token index from a timestamp-derived pseudo-random value.
block.timestamp is used as part of the randomness seed in setInitialTokenId.
msg.sender is used as part of the randomness seed in setInitialTokenId.
setInitialTokenId writes the derived value into the initialTokenId state variable.
mintable() relies on block.timestamp to compare against the configured mint date.
mintable() reads the mintDate struct as the comparison target.
wMintable() relies on block.timestamp to compare against the configured whitelist mint date.
wMintable() reads the wMintDate struct as the comparison target.
withdraw() performs a low-level send of the whole contract balance.
withdraw() sends the balance to msg.sender, the onlyOwner caller.
burn() checks ownerOf(_tokenId) == msg.sender before destroying the token.
burn() consumes the _tokenId parameter for the ownership check and burn.
tokenURI() computes finalTotenId from the queried token id.
initialTokenId shifts the metadata index computed in tokenURI.
setCost() consumes the _newCost parameter it writes to storage.
setMaxSupply() consumes the _newMaxSupply parameter it writes to storage.
setBaseURI() writes the caller-supplied _newBaseURI into the baseURI state variable.
setCost() updates the cost state variable used by the mint payment check.
setMaxSupply() updates the maxSupply state variable that bounds minting.
pause() toggles the paused state variable gating all mint paths.

normalization_plan.reason: The _to recipient parameter only exists as the input of mintInternal/_safeMint and should be absorbed into that core function.
_mintAmount is only consumed by mint() for the cost comparison and batch size, so it folds into the mint function node.
_tokenId only exists to drive the burn ownership check and destruction logic.
_newCost is a trivial setter argument fully captured by the setCost core function.
_newMaxSupply is a trivial setter argument fully captured by the setMaxSupply core function.
The loop index i has no meaning outside the mintInternal batch loop.
finalTotenId is a temporary value used only inside tokenURI for metadata index shifting.
